# Introduction

The objective of this notebook is to analyse the mIF data for FAP and CNN1 staining localisation

## Load packages

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Parameters

```{r}
# Paths
output_path <- "../03_output/01_vic_mIF_statistics/"
if(!dir.exists(output_path)) dir.create(output_path)

# Functions
source("../../utils.R")
```

```{r}
data <- read.csv("../01_data/mIF_VICs_measurements_full.csv")
colnames(data) <- c("Name", "Classification", "Area", "CNN1_Area", "FAP_Area")
head(data)
```

```{r}
# LMM on logit-transformed % area stained
# Replication unit = slide (8), repeated within slide across regions (3)
# Uses only segments that contain "Nodular Tissue"
# Regions kept: Inner Nodule, Peri-Nodular Margin (Inner Rim + Outer Rim), Other Tissue

# ---- helper: logit of a proportion with small offset and clamping
logit_pct <- function(pct, offset_pct = 0.001) {
  p <- (pct + offset_pct) / 100
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6)
  qlogis(p)
}

# ---- 1) Parse IDs and identify segments that have Nodular Tissue
data2 <- data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    slide_id   = stringr::str_extract(Name, "^[^-]+"),
    segment_id = stringr::str_extract(Name, "^[^-]+-\\d+")
  )

segments_with_nodule <- data2 %>%
  dplyr::filter(Classification == "Nodular Tissue") %>%
  dplyr::pull(segment_id) %>%
  unique()

# ---- 2) Keep only those segments and define the 3 regions of interest
df_roi <- data2 %>%
  dplyr::filter(segment_id %in% segments_with_nodule) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    region = dplyr::case_when(
      Classification == "Inner Nodule" ~ "Inner Nodule",
      Classification %in% c("Inner Rim", "Outer Rim") ~ "Peri-Nodular Margin",
      Classification == "Other Tissue" ~ "Other Tissue",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(region)) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    slide_id = factor(slide_id),
    region   = factor(region, levels = c("Inner Nodule", "Peri-Nodular Margin", "Other Tissue"))
  )

# ---- 3) Aggregate to slide × region and compute % stained for each marker
slide_region <- df_roi %>%
  dplyr::group_by(slide_id, region) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    Area_sum = sum(Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    FAP_sum  = sum(FAP_Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    CNN1_sum = sum(CNN1_Area, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Safety: stained <= total
    FAP_sum  = pmin(pmax(FAP_sum, 0), Area_sum),
    CNN1_sum = pmin(pmax(CNN1_sum, 0), Area_sum),
    FAP_percent  = 100 * FAP_sum  / Area_sum,
    CNN1_percent = 100 * CNN1_sum / Area_sum
  )

# Optional quick check: do you have all regions per slide?
# print(tidyr::pivot_wider(slide_region, names_from = region, values_from = Area_sum))

# ---- 4) Long format: one row per slide × region × antibody
df_long <- slide_region %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols      = c(FAP_percent, CNN1_percent),
    names_to  = "antibody",
    values_to = "pct_stained"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    antibody = dplyr::recode(antibody, FAP_percent = "FAP", CNN1_percent = "CNN1"),
    antibody = factor(antibody, levels = c("FAP", "CNN1")),
    logit_y  = logit_pct(pct_stained)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(logit_y))

# ---- 5) Fit LMM per antibody + emmeans + Holm posthoc + plot
results_lmm <- lapply(levels(droplevels(df_long$antibody)), function(ab) {

  ab_df <- df_long %>%
    dplyr::filter(antibody == ab) %>%
    droplevels()

  # Guardrails
  if (nrow(ab_df) == 0) {
    return(list(error = paste0("No rows for antibody = ", ab)))
  }
  if (nlevels(ab_df$region) < 2) {
    return(list(error = paste0("Need >=2 regions for antibody = ", ab),
                region_counts = table(ab_df$region)))
  }

  # LMM: region fixed effect, slide random intercept
  m <- lme4::lmer(logit_y ~ region + (1 | slide_id), data = ab_df, REML = FALSE)

  # Omnibus test for region (Satterthwaite df) via lmerTest
  a <- anova(m)

  # EMMs + Holm-adjusted contrasts on logit scale
  em <- emmeans::emmeans(m, ~ region)
  pw <- pairs(em, adjust = "holm")

  # Also provide EMMs back-transformed to % for interpretability
  em_df <- as.data.frame(em)
  em_df$pct_est <- 100 * plogis(em_df$emmean)  # inverse-logit to proportion, then %
  # approximate CI on % scale
  em_df$pct_lo  <- 100 * plogis(em_df$lower.CL)
  em_df$pct_hi  <- 100 * plogis(em_df$upper.CL)

  # Plot raw % by slide (spaghetti)
  p <- ggplot2::ggplot(ab_df, ggplot2::aes(x = region, y = pct_stained, group = slide_id)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = paste("Percent area stained –", ab),
      y     = "% stained area",
      x     = NULL
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

  list(model = m, anova = a, emmeans = em, emmeans_pct = em_df, pairs = pw, plot = p, data = ab_df)
})

names(results_lmm) <- levels(droplevels(df_long$antibody))

# ---- 6) Inspect results
results_lmm$FAP$anova
results_lmm$FAP$pairs
results_lmm$FAP$emmeans_pct
results_lmm$FAP$plot

results_lmm$CNN1$anova
results_lmm$CNN1$pairs
results_lmm$CNN1$emmeans_pct
results_lmm$CNN1$plot
```

```{r}

make_pairwise_table <- function(res, marker_name) {

  # Pairwise contrasts (already Holm-adjusted if you used adjust="holm" in pairs())
  pw <- as.data.frame(res$pairs) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      marker = marker_name,
      p_adj  = as.numeric(p.value)  # p.value column is already adjusted in your object
    )

  # Back-transformed EMMs (% stained) + CI
  means <- res$emmeans_pct %>%
    dplyr::select(region, pct_est, pct_lo, pct_hi) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(region = as.character(region))

  # Split contrast safely on " - " (NOT on "-" which appears inside Peri-Nodular)
  pw2 <- pw %>%
    tidyr::separate(
      contrast,
      into = c("region_1", "region_2"),
      sep = " - ",
      remove = FALSE
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      region_1 = stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_remove_all(region_1, "[()]")),
      region_2 = stringr::str_trim(stringr::str_remove_all(region_2, "[()]"))
    )

  # Join in region means for each side of the contrast
  out <- pw2 %>%
    dplyr::left_join(means, by = c("region_1" = "region")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(pct1 = pct_est, pct1_lo = pct_lo, pct1_hi = pct_hi) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(means, by = c("region_2" = "region")) %>%
    dplyr::rename(pct2 = pct_est, pct2_lo = pct_lo, pct2_hi = pct_hi) %>%
    # Nice rounding / formatting
    dplyr::mutate(
      estimate = round(estimate, 3),
      SE       = round(SE, 3),
      df       = round(df, 1),
      t.ratio  = round(t.ratio, 3),
      p_adj    = signif(p_adj, 3),

      pct1     = round(pct1, 3),
      pct1_lo  = round(pct1_lo, 3),
      pct1_hi  = round(pct1_hi, 3),
      pct2     = round(pct2, 3),
      pct2_lo  = round(pct2_lo, 3),
      pct2_hi  = round(pct2_hi, 3),

      # use plain "-" to avoid CSV/Excel encoding issues
      pct1_ci  = paste0(pct1, " (", pct1_lo, "-", pct1_hi, ")"),
      pct2_ci  = paste0(pct2, " (", pct2_lo, "-", pct2_hi, ")")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(
      marker, contrast,
      estimate, SE, df, t.ratio,
      p_adj,
      region_1, pct1_ci,
      region_2, pct2_ci
    )

  out
}

# ---- Example usage with your existing results_lmm object ----
tbl_fap  <- make_pairwise_table(results_lmm$FAP,  "FAP")
tbl_cnn1 <- make_pairwise_table(results_lmm$CNN1, "CNN1")

ihc_stats_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(tbl_fap, tbl_cnn1)

# View
ihc_stats_table

# --- Save as CSV
write.csv(ihc_stats_table, paste0(output_path, "mIF_region_LMM_pairwise_with_means.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```
